chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id who said:

I and Ibn Ghaylan al-Madaini went to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him). Ibn Ghaylan said to him: 'May God keep you well! It has reached me that whoever has a pregnancy and intends to name [the child] Muhammad, a boy will be born for him.'
He (the Imam) said: 'Whoever has a pregnancy and intends to name him Ali, a boy will be born for him.' Then he said: 'Ali [is] Muhammad and Muhammad [is] Ali — they are one thing.'

He (Ibn Ghaylan) said: 'May God keep you well! I have left my wife behind and she is pregnant. Supplicate to God that He make [the child] a boy.' So he (the Imam) bowed his head toward the ground for a long time, then raised his head and said to him: 'Name him Ali, for it will be a prolongation of his life.'
So we entered Mecca, and a letter came to us from al-Mada'in that a boy had been born for him.

key_terms.أصلحك الله: A du'a formula meaning 'May God rectify/keep you well,' used as respectful address to the Imam
key_terms.أطرق: Bowed his head in deep contemplation or prayer — indicates the Imam was seeking divine guidance
key_terms.حمل: Pregnancy, specifically referring to an unborn child
key_terms.عمر: Lifespan, age — the Imam's instruction ties the name Ali to longevity
key_terms.نوى: Intended, made the intention (niyyah) — connected to the theological principle that intention shapes outcomes

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about naming a child Ali or Muhammad to ensure a male birth?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts al-Husayn ibn Sa'id accompanying Ibn Ghaylan al-Madaini to visit Imam al-Ridha (AS). Ibn Ghaylan asked the Imam about the tradition that intending to name an unborn child Muhammad ensures a male birth. The Imam extended this to the name Ali as well, and then made the profound theological declaration that Ali and Muhammad are one and the same reality. When Ibn Ghaylan requested a supplication for a male child, the Imam — after prolonged contemplation — instructed him to name the child Ali for longevity. The narrative concludes with the confirmation of the Imam's prediction: a boy was indeed born. This hadith reflects the deep spiritual interconnection between the names Ali and Muhammad in Shia theological thought and demonstrates the Imam's charismatic authority and intercessory capacity.
